html:
The Western Desert cultural bloc is the name for the Aboriginal peoples of Australia's great central and western deserts, who share one language and one body of law across some 600,000 square kilometres.

They speak dialects of a single Western Desert language, part of the Pama-Nyungan family. Among them are the Pitjantjatjara and Yankunytjatjara around Uluru, the Ngaanyatjarra, the Pintupi, the Martu, the Luritja, the Kokatha and the Antakirinja.

Small family groups moved between rockholes and soakages, linked by wide networks of kin and by the Tjukurpa, or Dreaming, whose songlines run for hundreds of kilometres.

Contact came late. British atomic tests in the 1950s fell on Anangu land. In 1971 painters at Papunya began the Western Desert art movement, and in 1984 a Pintupi family who had never met settlers walked in from the desert.
sum: The Western Desert cultural bloc is the name for the Aboriginal peoples of Australia's great central and western deserts, who share one language and one body of law across some 600,000 square kilometres.
